svg.data-what: lung tissue at the end of the airways: alveoli opening off alveolar ducts, capillaries in their walls

path.data-what: alveolar sacs packed together: alveoli sharing their walls around the ends of the alveolar ducts

g.data-what: capillaries running in every wall between alveoli, so that blood passes within a micrometre of the air
the air spaces: the alveolar ducts and the alveoli opening off them

path.data-what: an alveolar duct, branching, its walls made of the mouths of alveoli

g.data-what: the alveolar walls: so thin where air meets blood, less than a micrometre, that gases cross by diffusion
type I cells: flat cells covering most of the alveolar surface, thin enough for gases to cross
type II cells, in the corners: they make surfactant, which keeps the alveoli from collapsing, and renew type I cells

path.data-what: a terminal bronchiole, the last airway that only conducts air, opening into the alveolar ducts

use.data-what: an alveolar macrophage, roaming the air spaces and swallowing dust and microbes

path.data-what: oxygen diffusing from the air into the blood of the capillary
carbon dioxide diffusing from the blood into the air, to be breathed out
